<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="מנחם אב_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919663_theRebbe_89" batchId="meluket-_D7_9E_D7_A0_D7_97_D7_9D_20_D7_90_D7_91_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919663_theRebbe_89__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>When service in the three lines is lacking due to sin, it affects even the essence of the soul, requiring redemption for the aspect of Tzion through Torah and for the captive soul-powers through charity.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">However,</t>
    <t s="2">when there is a deficiency in the service of the aforementioned three lines,</t>
    <t s="3">because of our sins,</t>
    <t s="4">although the matter of sin is from the aspect of the soul that is clothed in the body,</t>
    <t s="5">nevertheless, this also affects the essence of the soul.</t>
    <t s="6">As it is written,</t>
    <t s="7">"Return, O Israel, to the Lord your God, for you have stumbled in your iniquity,"</t>
    <t s="8">for the one who stumbles in action is the foot, and "Israel" is the letters "Li Rosh" (a head to Me),</t>
    <t s="9">the head of the soul,</t>
    <t s="10">and it says "Return, O Israel,"</t>
    <t s="11">because the stumbling of the foot of the soul affects even the aspect of the soul above.</t>
    <t s="12">This is like a person who stumbles with his foot,</t>
    <t s="13">whereby his head also falls.</t>
    <t s="14">And this is the concept of "Tzion shall be redeemed through justice,"</t>
    <t s="15">that the aspect of Tzion,</t>
    <t s="16">the essence of the soul called Tzion,</t>
    <t s="17">requires redemption from the things that cover it,</t>
    <t s="18">which prevent the revelation in the soul that is in the body.</t>
    <t s="19">That is, the redemption that must occur in the aspect of Tzion is not a redemption from captivity,</t>
    <t s="20">for in the essence of the soul, the concept of captivity, heaven forbid, does not apply,</t>
    <t s="21">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="22">"And My glory I will not give to another,"</t>
    <t s="23">where "My glory"</t>
    <t s="24">refers to the aspect of the innerness of Malchus,</t>
    <t s="25">and in man this is the concept of the innerness of the heart,</t>
    <t s="26">the innerness of the soul, even to the aspect of the essence of the soul,</t>
    <t s="27">that this aspect "I will not give to another,"</t>
    <t s="28">and the concept of redemption that must occur in the aspect of Tzion is only the departure from the things that cover it, as above.</t>
    <t s="29">[See what is explained in Igeres HaKodesh,</t>
    <t s="30">and in the discourses on the verse,</t>
    <t s="31">"He redeemed my soul in peace," regarding the redemption of the general Shechinah from exile and regarding the redemption of each particular spark of the Shechinah in the soul of every Jew, and specifically through peace.]</t>
    <t s="32">And this redemption is through justice,</t>
    <t s="33">that is, through the Torah,</t>
    <t s="34">for through engagement in Torah, the aspect of the innerness of the heart is revealed.</t>
    <t s="35">But in order to redeem from exile the powers of the soul</t>
    <t s="36">(which are in the clothing of the body)</t>
    <t s="37">that are truly captive,</t>
    <t s="38">it requires specifically charity,</t>
    <t s="39">"and her captives [shall be redeemed] through charity."</t>
    <t s="40">And by redeeming them from captivity,</t>
    <t s="41">there is thereby a superiority of light in ultimate perfection,</t>
    <t s="42">like the parable of a king's son who, when he is always in his father's house,</t>
    <t s="43">the joy is not so intense,</t>
    <t s="44">but when the king's son was in captivity and grinding in the prison house, etc., and goes free to his father's house, the king,</t>
    <t s="45">then specifically the joy becomes very great, and both rejoice with great and immense joy.</t>
    <t s="46">And analogous to the well-known concept</t>
    <t s="47">regarding the greatness of the joy that will be in the future in the time of the three weeks,</t>
    <t s="48">and especially in the nine days,</t>
    <t s="49">and especially in the days of the Seventeenth of Tammuz and Tisha B'Av,</t>
    <t s="50">that the joy of these festivals</t>
    <t s="51">[that these days will be turned into joy and gladness and good festivals]</t>
    <t s="52">will be a great joy with surpassing excellence and strength beyond the joy of the festivals in the usual manner.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The reason the redemption of the soul's essence is through Torah (justice) and the redemption of the captive soul-powers is through charity (mitzvos) is because Torah itself is never truly captive, while mitzvos, being clothed in physicality, can be captured.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the essence of the matter and one of the reasons that the redemption of the aspect of the essence of the soul is through justice, which is Torah,</t>
    <t s="2">and the redemption of the aspect of the soul-powers that came into captivity is through charity, which is the totality of the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="3">is because Torah and mitzvos themselves are also analogous to these two concepts.</t>
    <t s="4">For behold, the Torah, even as it descended below,</t>
    <t s="5">and even when it is studied by an impure person,</t>
    <t s="6">is as it is above,</t>
    <t s="7">the word of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="8">as per the exposition of our sages, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="9">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="10">"Behold, My word is like fire."</t>
    <t s="11">And since the Torah is not in a state of clothing,</t>
    <t s="12">therefore the concept of captivity, heaven forbid, does not apply to it.</t>
    <t s="13">Nevertheless, the concept of redemption does apply to it,</t>
    <t s="14">for due to the things through which it descended</t>
    <t s="15">(even though it is not clothed in them),</t>
    <t s="16">it can be in a state of concealment.</t>
    <t s="17">However, the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="18">since they are clothed in physical objects,</t>
    <t s="19">tzitzis in physical wool, tefillin in physical parchment, etc., and even the mitzvos of the heart's duties must be felt in the physical brain and heart,</t>
    <t s="20">therefore the concept of captivity applies to them,</t>
    <t s="21">as explained elsewhere regarding the verse,</t>
    <t s="22">"I rejoice over Your word like one who finds great spoil,"</t>
    <t s="23">that in mitzvos there is the concept of spoil,</t>
    <t s="24">meaning that they plunder and extract from the other side.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>These two concepts—redemption of Tzion through Torah and redemption of captives through charity—exist in every Jew individually and in the collective, corresponding to the righteous and baalei teshuvah, with the latter requiring charity in the era of the footsteps of Moshiach.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, these two concepts</t>
    <t s="2">(the aspect of "Tzion shall be redeemed through justice" and the aspect of "her captives through charity")</t>
    <t s="3">exist in all three aspects of world, year, and soul.</t>
    <t s="4">And in the aspect of soul, they exist</t>
    <t s="5">both in each individual Jew and in the collective of Israel</t>
    <t s="6">[for since each individual Jew is a complete world,</t>
    <t s="7">it is understood that the concepts in each individual Jew exist also in the collective of Israel, and the concepts in the collective of Israel exist also in each individual Jew].</t>
    <t s="8">For each individual Jew,</t>
    <t s="9">by virtue of his service in the line of Torah, is in the aspect of "Tzion shall be redeemed through justice,"</t>
    <t s="10">and by virtue of his service in the line of mitzvos, he is in the aspect of "her captives through charity."</t>
    <t s="11">And likewise in the collective of Israel,</t>
    <t s="12">who are divided into two types: Yissachar and Zevulun,</t>
    <t s="13">masters of Torah and masters of good deeds.</t>
    <t s="14">For the masters of Torah are in the aspect of "Tzion shall be redeemed through justice,"</t>
    <t s="15">and the masters of good deeds are in the aspect of "her captives through charity."</t>
    <t s="16">And more generally,</t>
    <t s="17">this is the distinction between the righteous and baalei teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="18">For regarding the righteous, the concept of captivity, heaven forbid, does not apply, for no harm befalls the righteous,</t>
    <t s="19">and certainly regarding the righteous who are in the aspect of "my heart is hollow within me."</t>
    <t s="20">Nevertheless, even for them the concept of redemption applies,</t>
    <t s="21">in the manner that sometimes the righteous person is seized for the sin of the generation,</t>
    <t s="22">or as it is written regarding Moshe, "Go down, for your people have corrupted themselves,"</t>
    <t s="23">that because "your people have corrupted themselves," a descent occurred</t>
    <t s="24">also for him,</t>
    <t s="25">but nevertheless, since the descent</t>
    <t s="26">(and even when he is seized for the sin of the generation)</t>
    <t s="27">is only due to matters external to him,</t>
    <t s="28">therefore even then he is not in captivity, heaven forbid, for the essence of the righteous is a sign</t>
    <t s="29">(of G-dliness)</t>
    <t s="30">in the world,</t>
    <t s="31">so to speak,</t>
    <t s="32">just as G-dliness is below,</t>
    <t s="33">for his existence</t>
    <t s="34">(of the righteous)</t>
    <t s="35">is that he is an agent of the Supernal Man,</t>
    <t s="36">and a person's agent is like himself.</t>
    <t s="37">Therefore,</t>
    <t s="38">even when he is in a state of descent, etc.,</t>
    <t s="39">his redemption is through the Torah.</t>
    <t s="40">For in the Torah,</t>
    <t s="41">this concept</t>
    <t s="42">(that even below it is G-dliness in revelation,</t>
    <t s="43">as above regarding "Behold, My word is like fire")</t>
    <t s="44">is more revealed.</t>
    <t s="45">However, the baalei teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="46">whose service is to extract the sparks that fell and were captured in the other side</t>
    <t s="47">(analogous—in holiness—to "and he took captive from them a captive"),</t>
    <t s="48">therefore their redemption must also be analogous to this.</t>
    <t s="49">And this is "her captives through charity,"</t>
    <t s="50">that their redemption is in the line of charity,</t>
    <t s="51">which is the totality of the mitzvos</t>
    <t s="52">[for the entire body is included in the right],</t>
    <t s="53">for the service of the line of mitzvos is in a manner of captivity and spoil.</t>
    <t s="54">And as explained in Igeres HaKodesh,</t>
    <t s="55">that the main service of G-d in these times of the footsteps of Moshiach is the service of charity</t>
    <t s="56">(unlike in the time of the Talmud,</t>
    <t s="57">when Torah study was their main service),</t>
    <t s="58">for in order to raise the fallen Sukkah of Dovid to the aspect of feet and heels, which is the aspect of Asiyah, the service must specifically be in the aspect of Asiyah,</t>
    <t s="59">which is the deed of charity.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
